Option picker

Exactly one of up to about ten options, each a full-width row with a name, a one-line description and an optional state in words, built on native radios.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • To choose exactly one of two to about ten options where each needs more than a label: a repository and its path, an agent and the model it runs, a mode and what it allows.
  • When some options cannot be chosen right now and the reader should still see them and the reason, such as Signed out or Usage limit reached.
  • When one option carries a risk the reader should weigh before choosing it, such as running commands without asking.
  • When the last option lets the reader type a value that is not in the list, such as a path, in a field shown under it.

When not to use it

  • For options that a short label names by itself, with at most a line of help. Use a radio group.
  • For two to five options of one or two words each. Use a segmented control.
  • For more than about ten options, or a list the reader scans rather than reads. Use a select, or a combobox when typing is faster.
  • For a choice that should stay on screen as a selection the app's script manages, with several selectable or with keys of its own. Use a listbox.
  • For a setting that takes effect the moment it changes, among other settings on a page. Use a settings row, with a select or a switch.

Variants

description
The name and a ds-option-picker__description under it, one line that says what the option does.
path
The description holds ds-option-picker__path, with the folders in ds-option-picker__start and the last folder in ds-option-picker__end. The path stays on one line and loses its middle.
state
ds-option-picker__state after ds-option-picker__text, a state in words such as Signed out. Below 768px it sits under the text; from 768px it is at the trailing end of the row, level with the name.
warning ds-option-picker__state--warning
On ds-option-picker__state, for a risk of the option in a word or a short phrase, such as Runs commands without asking. The stylesheet draws a warning icon and the warning tone.
reveal
A div with ds-option-picker__reveal straight after an option's label. It is shown only while that option is chosen, such as a ds-field for a path after an Enter a path option.

Accessibility

  • Use a fieldset with ds-option-picker and a legend with ds-option-picker__legend that names the choice. An optional hint is a p with ds-option-picker__hint after the legend, and the fieldset points at it with aria-describedby.
  • Each option is a label with ds-option-picker__option that wraps the whole row, so a press anywhere on it chooses the option. Inside it comes input type="radio" with ds-option-picker__input first, then a span with ds-option-picker__body holding a span with ds-option-picker__text (the ds-option-picker__name and an optional ds-option-picker__description) and an optional span with ds-option-picker__state.
  • Name the input with aria-labelledby pointing at its ds-option-picker__name, and point aria-describedby at its state and description, so a screen reader reads the name, then the state and the description, and not all of it as one name.
  • Every input in a group has the same name attribute, different from every other group on the page.
  • A path is written in full in ds-option-picker__start and ds-option-picker__end, with no white space between them. The stylesheet cuts the middle from view only, so the description read aloud keeps the whole path.
  • An option that cannot be chosen takes the disabled attribute on its input. It stays in the list, and its ds-option-picker__state says why in words, with its description saying what to do. Its text keeps a contrast pair of the system.
  • A warning is ds-option-picker__state with ds-option-picker__state--warning: the words say the risk, and the stylesheet adds the icon, so the tone is never the only signal.
  • A ds-option-picker__reveal is shown by the stylesheet while the option before it is checked, with no script, and is out of the tab order while hidden. Do not put required on a control inside it; check it when the form is sent.
  • For an error, the fieldset takes role="radiogroup", aria-labelledby pointing at the legend, aria-required="true", aria-invalid="true" and aria-describedby pointing at a p with ds-option-picker__error after the last option, and at the hint too when there is one. The message says what to do, and its icon is drawn by the stylesheet.
  • Tab moves into the group, to the chosen option or the first one. The arrow keys move between options, skip a disabled one and choose as they go, and Space chooses the focused option. All of it comes from the native inputs.
  • Each row is at least 44px tall and as wide as the group, and the mark has a 44px target of its own inside it.
